field.label: Source
field.help:
"any", devices, IPs/subnets and/or firewall aliases, mixed.
Devices (picked from the DHCP leases and ARP table, or type a MAC such as aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff) are matched by MAC address: App Router keeps a firewall alias of type "MAC address" per rule (ar_<id>_mac, do not edit) that core resolves to the device's current IP, so the rule follows the device when its IP changes.
  • Apple devices: set "Private Wi-Fi Address" to Fixed or Off for this network, otherwise the MAC changes (devices marked "private (random) MAC").
  • Matching starts only once the device's IP is in the ARP table, about 5 minutes after it joins.
  • IPv4 only.
  • WireGuard peers have no MAC: use their tunnel IP (e.g. 10.10.0.2).
IPs/subnets: type and press Enter (192.168.1.0/24, 10.0.0.5). Aliases are referenced as pf tables, changes to an alias apply without touching the rule.

field.label: App Categories
field.help: Search and select app categories or individual apps

field.label: Custom Domains
field.help: Comma-separated domains (e.g. example.com, cdn.test.org). All subdomains matched automatically.

field.label: Resolve DNS via Gateway
field.help:
Resolve the domains of this rule (categories and custom domains) through the rule's gateway, using the DNS server below.
Use it when a site still sends you to its international version, or refuses service, although its traffic goes through the gateway: many CDNs choose the server by the location of the DNS resolver, not of the client.
  • Applies to all clients that resolve these domains through Unbound, not only to this rule's sources.
  • Lookups take a little longer and fail while the gateway is down.
  • DNS servers in front of Unbound (e.g. AdGuard Home) must forward these domains to Unbound; the list is in /usr/local/etc/app-router/dns_via_gateway.txt.

field.label: DNS Server
field.help: Public DNS server in the gateway's region, queried over TCP port 53, e.g. 223.6.6.6 (AliDNS) or 119.29.29.29 (DNSPod) for China. App Router routes this address through the gateway, so pick one your other DNS settings don't use.

field.label: Gateway
field.help: The exit this traffic leaves through. While it is gone (disabled, deleted, its interface missing) the traffic is blocked, it never leaves another way.
